maml:description.maml:para: Finds dynamic membership rules that use the memberOf operator before it is retired

Microsoft Entra ID is retiring the memberOf operator in dynamic membership rules. After November 3, 2026, dynamic membership groups, dynamic administrative units and entitlement management auto-assignment policies that use it stop updating and stay in their last known state. This command finds every rule that uses it, so an admin can replace the rule or convert the object to assigned membership before that date.
Three sources feed the same scanner:
Rule text (-Rule) scans one or more rules given as strings, which is the quickest way to check a rule before saving it.
File mode (-Path) scans a CSV or JSON export: the admin center's dynamic group export, or a saved Graph response. Columns are matched by name (membershipRule or rule, id or objectId, displayName or name, and an optional object kind), so most exports work as they are.
Tenant mode (-Tenant) reads every dynamic membership group, every dynamic administrative unit and every auto-assignment policy in the connected tenant through Microsoft Graph, resolves the display name of each source group, and reports groups whose source groups are themselves memberOf groups. It needs Microsoft.Graph.Authentication and an existing Connect-MgGraph session; every call is a GET and the command never writes to the tenant.
The scanner tokenizes each rule rather than searching its text, so a rule that only mentions memberOf inside a quoted value is not reported as using the operator. Each result's Level is Retired (the rule uses user.memberOf or device.memberOf), Review (memberOf appears some other way, or the rule could not be read to the end; ReviewCode says which) or Clean. In tenant and file mode a summary object follows the results, whose Outcome keeps "nothing found" apart from "not everything was read".
[String[]] (Mandatory in file mode, Pipeline: ByPropertyName as FullName)
One or more .csv or .json files. Wildcards are allowed. Every row becomes one result; a file with no recognizable rule column is an error, because it cannot be scanned and must not come back clean.
Replaces the Graph call. Receives the URI and a headers hashtable and returns the parsed body. Exists so tests can run tenant mode with no tenant; production callers leave it unset.
[String[]] (Mandatory in rule mode, Pipeline: ByValue, ByPropertyName as MembershipRule)
One or more membership rules as text. Each becomes one result of ObjectKind Rule.
Do not resolve source group display names. Saves one request per fifteen distinct source group ids.
Read the connected tenant over Microsoft Graph. Needs a Connect-MgGraph session with Group.Read.All, AdministrativeUnit.Read.All and EntitlementManagement.Read.All, or a subset matching -ObjectKind.

Rule text, bound by value to -Rule. Objects with a MembershipRule property, such as a group read from Graph, bind to -Rule by property name; objects with a FullName property, such as the output of Get-ChildItem, bind to -Path.

One per rule-bearing object. ObjectKind (Group, AdministrativeUnit, AutoAssignmentPolicy or Rule), Id, DisplayName, AccessPackageName, RuleKind (user or device), Level (Retired, Review or Clean), ReviewCode, ProcessingState, Rule, Quantifier, Operator, SourceGroupIds, SourceGroupNames, DependsOnMemberOfGroup, DependsOn, Remediation, Note, Source and Error.

One per scan in tenant and file mode, after the results. Outcome (Retired, Review, Incomplete or Clean), Coverage, Mode, per-kind Groups, AdministrativeUnits, AutoAssignmentPolicies and Rules counts with their Coverage, MemberOfGroupCount, MemberOfGroupLimit, DependencyChainCount, RetiredCount, ReviewCount, RetirementDate, IncompleteKinds and Message.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```powershell Test-EntraMemberOfRule -Rule "user.memberOf -any (group.objectId -in ['a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001'])" | Format-List Level, RuleKind, Quantifier, Operator, SourceGroupIds, Remediation ```

```Output Level : Retired RuleKind : user Quantifier : any Operator : in SourceGroupIds : {a1b2c3d4-0000-4000-8000-000000000001} Remediation : Replace memberOf with a supported rule operator, or convert the object to assigned membership, then validate the result. ```
Scans a rule given as text, for instance one pasted into a ticket, and reports what it uses. Rule text mode emits one result per rule and no summary.

command:example.maml:title: --------- Example 2: Scan the admin center's dynamic group export ---------

maml:introduction.maml:para: ```Output ObjectKind DisplayName Level RuleKind State Chain SourceGroups ---------- ----------- ----- -------- ----- ----- ------------ Group All Sales Clean On Group Sales and Marketing Retired user On All Sales, All Marketing Group Rollup of Rollups Retired user Paused yes Sales and Marketing Group Says memberOf Review On

Outcome : Retired Coverage : Complete Mode : File Groups : Complete: 4 scanned, 2 retired, 1 review ... Message : 2 object(s) use memberOf and stop updating after November 3, 2026; 1 more need a look. ```

Every row becomes one result, then a summary follows. Source group names are taken from the file itself when the source group is in it. Chain marks a memberOf group whose source is another memberOf group, which the Learn page lists as unsupported.

```Output ObjectKind DisplayName Level RuleKind State Chain SourceGroups ---------- ----------- ----- -------- ----- ----- ------------ Group EntraMemberOf-Rollup Retired user On EntraMemberOf-Source Group EntraMemberOf-Nested Retired user On yes EntraMemberOf-Rollup, 00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000... Group SC300-myDynamicGroup Clean On AdministrativeUnit EntraMemberOf-AU Retired user On EntraMemberOf-Source

Outcome : Retired Coverage : Complete Mode : Tenant Groups : Complete: 3 scanned, 2 retired, 0 review AdministrativeUnits : Complete: 1 scanned, 1 retired, 0 review AutoAssignmentPolicies : Complete: 0 scanned, 0 retired, 0 review ... Message : 3 object(s) use memberOf and stop updating after November 3, 2026. ```

Reads every dynamic membership group, dynamic administrative unit and auto-assignment policy rule through Microsoft Graph, following every page, then resolves source group names. Chain marks a memberOf group whose source is itself a memberOf group; a source id that no longer exists is kept and named in the Note. A kind that cannot be read is reported with Write-Error and the summary's Coverage says Incomplete, so a missing permission never turns into a clean result.
